criteria.label: llms.txt published
criteria.what: A plain-text file at /llms.txt that lists the site's important pages for AI assistants.
criteria.how: Request https://DOMAIN/llms.txt. Counts only if the response is real plain text. A page of HTML, a redirect to the homepage, or a 404 does not count.

criteria.label: Runs its own tracking software
criteria.what: The agency operates its own named software for tracking AI visibility, that a client can log into — rather than reselling somebody else's tool or sending a PDF.
criteria.how: Look for a named product with its own product page AND a working customer login or signup. Naming a third-party tool (Semrush, Ahrefs, Profound, Peec, Otterly, Scrunch) does not count. An internal "framework" or "methodology" the agency's own team runs does not count — the client has to be able to log in.

criteria.label: Names the AI engines it covers
criteria.what: A public page names at least three specific AI engines the agency works on, so a buyer knows what they are paying for.
criteria.how: Look for at least three of: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Copilot, Claude, Grok, Meta AI, DeepSeek, Mistral, Alexa, Siri. Saying "AI search engines" or "LLMs" in general does not count. If a site's bot protection stops an automated client reading the page, it does not count — an AI cannot read it either.

criteria.label: robots.txt names AI crawlers
criteria.what: The robots.txt file names AI crawlers by name and says what they may do, instead of leaving them to a catch-all rule.
criteria.how: Read https://DOMAIN/robots.txt and look for any of: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, CCBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, Bytespider, Amazonbot. Full points only if at least one is named and none of the eleven is denied site-wide access. A rule blocking a single path, such as an API directory, is not site-wide denial.

criteria.label: Price readable by a machine
criteria.what: A real price for the agency's own work sits inside a plain-text file an AI can read, not only inside a web page.
criteria.how: Look for a dollar figure for their own service inside /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt or /agents.md on their own domain. A price on an HTML page only does not count — that is the whole point of the check.

criteria.label: llms-full.txt published
criteria.what: The long version of llms.txt: the site's actual content in one text file, so an AI can read it without crawling.
criteria.how: Request https://DOMAIN/llms-full.txt. Same rule: plain text only.

criteria.label: agents.md published
criteria.what: A file that tells AI agents who the business is and what it is allowed to be quoted on.
criteria.how: Request https://DOMAIN/agents.md. Same rule: plain text only.

criteria.label: Prices published
criteria.what: A real dollar figure for their own work is on a public page. "Contact us for a quote" does not count.
criteria.how: Check the homepage, /pricing, and any pricing link in the navigation. The figure has to be attached to their own service, not to a client's result or an industry average. Any public URL on their own domain counts, including a text file — one agency publishes its minimum fee only inside llms.txt, and it scores.

criteria.label: Team named on their own site
criteria.what: At least one real person, named, on the agency's own website.
criteria.how: Check the homepage, /about and /team, and any public text file on their own domain. LinkedIn does not count. People quoted as clients in testimonials are not that agency's staff.

criteria.label: Case studies name the client
criteria.what: Published work that names the actual client, not "a B2B SaaS company".
criteria.how: Check the case studies or results page for at least one named client.

criteria.label: Case studies carry a number
criteria.what: At least one published result with a specific figure attached.
criteria.how: Check the same pages for a stated percentage, dollar figure or multiple.

criteria.label: You can buy without a sales call
criteria.what: A visitor can start paying, or start a free trial, without booking a call or filling in a lead form first.
criteria.how: Look for a public signup, a checkout, a "start free trial", or a plan button that leads to creating an account. "Book a call", "Get a proposal", "Request a quote", "Contact us" and a "free audit" that is really a form all count as no.
